What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH001Optional passwordless auto-login for test environmentsKTPH002 — a new KTPH003Configuration → Global Settings → Security → Disable master password prompt on startupKTPH004 option makes korTTY remember the master password (stored only obfuscated, with owner-only permissions, in KTPH000) and unlock the vault automatically at startup, so encrypted data such as AI profiles and SSH passwords stays usable with no prompt. On a brand-new profile it even sets up a default password so the app can start with zero input. It is insecure by design — the file permissions are the only protection — and meant for throwaway/test setups such as a VM: korTTY asks you to confirm before enabling it, keeps a warning visible while it is on, and an enterprise policy that forces the master password overrides it. Off by default.

KTPH000The offline guide can now be translated by a local AI profileKTPH001 — KTPH002Configuration → Global Settings → Translation → Guide translationKTPH003 translates the bundled offline guide (the same site this documentation is part of), including its in-page search, into the target language chosen above, using an AI profile rather than the translation-provider API. Translation runs in the background: it keeps going after Settings is closed, shows a progress bar, percentage and time-remaining estimate at the right end of the menu bar, can be cancelled and resumed without losing progress, and korTTY asks before quitting while it is running. After an update that changed the guide, korTTY offers once to bring an existing translation up to date, re-translating only what actually changed. See KTPH004TranslationKTPH005.

KTPH000Estimate duration before committing to a full translationKTPH001 — a new KTPH002Estimate durationKTPH003 button measures the chosen AI profile against a real sample of the guide and projects how long translating everything remaining would take, without waiting out the full run.

KTPH000A warning appears before translating with a reasoning modelKTPH001 — such models spend most of their output "thinking" rather than translating, which can turn a translation that takes about an hour into one that takes six or more; korTTY detects this from the model's name and warns before starting or estimating, while still allowing you to proceed.

KTPH000Any AI profile can now translate the interface stringsKTPH001 — the KTPH002Local AI text profileKTPH003 provider gained its own KTPH004AI profileKTPH005 dropdown, matching the one the guide translation already had. A profile picked there is used whatever its connection mode, so a cloud model (Anthropic, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) or a local CLI profile can generate a language pack, not only an embedded llama.cpp/MLX model. Leaving it on KTPH006Default (local text profile)KTPH007 keeps the previous behaviour: the Text-role profile, and only when it runs a local model — the provider exists for people who do not want their interface strings leaving the machine. When that role holds a cloud or CLI profile, korTTY now names the profile and points at the dropdown instead of reporting a bare "failed to generate language file". See KTPH008TranslationKTPH009.

KTPH000A malformed batch no longer throws away the whole language packKTPH001 — previously one bad reply from the model aborted language-file generation completely and nothing was written at all, even though most strings had translated. The batch is now retried and split in half, and only a string the model never returns in usable form keeps its English text.

KTPH000Management tools can open as tabs in the main windowKTPH001 — a new KTPH002Open tool windows as tabsKTPH003 option in KTPH004Window settingsKTPH005 makes Snippets, the JobScheduler, the AI Manager, Saved Chats, Credential/GPG/SSH key management, the Video Manager, Teamwork settings and the Terminal Effects manager open as tabs beside your terminal sessions instead of separate windows. The tab always opens in the main window whose menu you used, so with several windows open each collects its own tools — for example the AI Manager as a tab in one window and the JobScheduler in another. Reopening a tool focuses its existing tab, while the snippet editor and the AI code analysis open a new tab per snippet/run so several can sit side by side; tool tabs can be reordered and dragged between windows like any other tab. Off by default — nothing changes unless you enable it.

KTPH003New: the AI can build input validation directly into your scriptsKTPH004 — every AI script flow (Full code analysis, Improve robustness, Custom improvement, and both workflow-script generators) gained an opt-in KTPH005Input hardeningKTPH006 panel. When enabled, the AI adds a guard block at the top of the generated or rewritten script that validates every parameter (count, character allowlists, length limits, rejection of shell metacharacters), checks input files before use (existence, text-vs-binary format, and a size limit generated as an adjustable KTPH000 script variable, 10 MB by default), and reports every violation as a timestamped KTPH001 warning on stderr and in the script's own log file. Violations stop the script with documented exit codes (64/65/66) unless a run is deliberately forced with KTPH002 — which still logs the bypass. korTTY itself performs no validation at run time: the guard is ordinary script code, so it protects every future run of the script, wherever it is started. KTPH007AllKTPH008/KTPH009ClearKTPH010/KTPH011SaveKTPH012 manage the five sub-options, and KTPH013SaveKTPH014 remembers your selection and size limit as the default. See KTPH015Input hardeningKTPH016.

KTPH000Selection translation and spelling correction no longer fail on small local reasoning modelsKTPH001 — the snippet editor's KTPH002Translate selection…KTPH003 and KTPH004Correct spelling in selectionKTPH005 actions were attaching your enabled AI skills to the request. On a compact local reasoning model (for example a quantized Phi-4-mini reasoning build) the extra prompt bulk could make the model spend its whole reply on internal reasoning and return no answer (KTPH006"the local AI model produced no answer"KTPH007). These two mechanical text transforms no longer attach AI skills, keeping the prompt small so the model answers.

KTPH000A long AI request is no longer cut off after three minutesKTPH001 — a request through a provider CLI, or through LM Studio's native API with an MCP internet mode, aborted after a hardcoded 180 seconds (Anthropic profiles after 120), which was easy to hit with the snippet editor's KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 on a large snippet. korTTY no longer imposes any timeout of its own; requests run until the model answers. If you do want a limit, set one yourself in KTPH004AI → AI Manager → ProfilesKTPH005: KTPH006AI request timeoutKTPH007 in minutes applies to every profile, and KTPH008Timeout for this profileKTPH009 overrides it for a single profile — including setting it to 0 so that one profile never times out. See KTPH010AI settingsKTPH011.

Only the current release is listed here, so the guide stays short in every language it is translated into. Every version is on the KTPH002GitHub releases pageKTPH003; the curated notes for earlier versions are kept in the repository, in KTPH000 and KTPH001.
